clue.text: Is this what a door-to-door salesman is looking for where there are no exports?

definitions.text: Is this what a door-to-door salesman is looking for where there are no exports?

parts.words: Is this what a door-to-door salesman is looking for where there are no exports?
parts.note: a trade term for selling within one's own country is read literally as a market made of households, which is exactly what a doorstep seller canvasses

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a travelling salesman seeks when nothing goes abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The economic phrase for domestic trade (no exports) doubles as a description of the doorstep seller's customers: the people in their houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means domestic trade within a country, as opposed to overseas sales, and literally a market of householders.

clue.text: Fish entered highly explosive cover

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the fish is placed within the explosive letters

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive
the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A fish swims into something dangerous to find shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' puts IDE inside HE, giving H(IDE)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is a concealed shelter for watching birds or animals, so it acts as a screen or concealment.

clue.text: Island that is not completely messy

indicators.note: says the word for messy loses its final letter, so it is not given in full

parts.note: mucky means dirty or messy

explanation.surface: An island described as only partly untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' drops the last letter of MUCKY. Muck is one of the Small Isles in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Let him move from small place in fife

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made to shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to allow a man to relocate from a little Fife town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges LETHIM. Fife is a county on Scotland's east coast; Methil is a small town there on the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Methil is a small coastal town in the Scottish region of Fife.

clue.text: Tell a story and give one the bill for it?

definitions.meaning: to narrate or give a report of events

definitions.text: give one the bill for it?
definitions.meaning: to send someone an invoice requesting payment

explanation.surface: Someone narrates a tale and then charges the listener for the telling.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase covers both a verbal report and the commercial act of submitting an invoice; the question mark flags the second, jokier reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to give a report of events and to present a bill to a customer for payment.

clue.text: Partial problem, I liaised with Shakespearean character

indicators.note: Partial says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone discussing a problem and working alongside a figure from the plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'with', which is only the link joining wordplay to definition; the definition is 'Shakespearean character'. The run is probl(EM I LIA)ised.
explanation.definitionFit: Emilia is Iago's wife in Othello, one of several roles of that name in the playwright's works.

clue.text: Lady before time produced fat

indicators.note: the woman's name comes ahead of the letter for time in the answer

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman, ahead of schedule, made something greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Suet is hard animal fat used in British puddings and pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard white fat from around the kidneys of cattle and sheep, used in cooking.

clue.text: On the downward side the nude ran distraught

indicators.note: being upset or in a state, the three words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A naked person flees in a panic down the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' rearranges THENUDERAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath means below or on the lower surface, which is the side facing down.

clue.text: Mark to obey disconcertingly! That is satisfactory

parts.note: a tick is a mark made to show something is correct

indicators.note: upset or thrown into confusion, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a sign of approval says to comply, which oddly turns out fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcertingly' signals the anagram of 'to obey'. The answer is dated British slang meaning everything is in order; 'That is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This dated British colloquialism means fine, in good order or going well.

clue.text: Anyone on board for this game?

definitions.text: Anyone on board for this game?

parts.words: Anyone on board for this game?
parts.note: plays on the old catchphrase 'Anyone for tennis?' with 'on board' meaning on a ship's deck

explanation.surface: Someone asks if any passengers fancy playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyone for tennis?' is a stock line from drawing-room comedies; slipping in 'on board' moves the game onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a game played on a ship with a ring tossed over a net, a shipboard variant of the racket sport.

clue.text: Old pupil left in charge of poems

indicators.note: the pupil's letter has departed from the word old, so it is taken away

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A former schoolchild who has gone now runs the poetry department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old pupil' suggests a former student, but 'Old' is the word itself and 'left' means the learner's letter departs from it. L for pupil comes from the learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Odic is the adjective relating to odes, which are lyric verses.

clue.text: Chamber for spontaneous reaction?

parts.note: names the word that goes before 'chamber' in an engine and after 'spontaneous' in a fire that starts itself

explanation.surface: A question about a room where something happens of its own accord.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer pairs with both 'chamber' (part of an engine) and 'spontaneous' (self-ignition), so the clue reads as a riddle about a room.
explanation.definitionFit: This is burning, the chemical reaction of a fuel with oxygen, as in an engine chamber or self-igniting haystack.

clue.text: Some players may be unsuited in this game

definitions.text: Some players may be unsuited in this game

parts.words: Some players may be unsuited in this game
parts.note: 'unsuited' looks like 'not right for it' but means losing one's clothes in a card game where garments are wagered

explanation.surface: A remark that certain players are ill-matched to a particular contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsuited' also hints at cards without matching suits, but the real sense is out of one's suit, undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a card game in which losers remove items of clothing.

clue.text: I had accompanied priest into foreign office during opera

indicators.note: the short form and the priest go inside the government department's letters

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the UK ministry for overseas affairs
I'd is the contraction of I had, written without the apostrophe
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised the boy Samuel

explanation.surface: Someone recounts taking a clergyman into a government department while an opera was on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanied' simply joins the contraction to the biblical priest, and 'into' places that pair within the ministry's initials; 'during' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera, about a wife who rescues her imprisoned husband.

clue.text: Angle to get some profit from stockings

definitions.note: the answer names a mesh fabric used for such hosiery, often called by its name in the plural

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
net is profit after deductions

explanation.surface: An angler hoping to make some money from selling hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get some' and 'from' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishnets are hosiery woven in an open diamond mesh, like a fishing net.

clue.text: Go too far and be swamped?

definitions.meaning: to exceed a limit or run beyond an intended stopping point
overwhelmed or infested in large numbers, as a garden by weeds

explanation.surface: A warning that exceeding limits leads to being overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense takes the past participle: a place swamped by invaders has been overrun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to exceed a limit and, as a participle, overwhelmed or invaded in great numbers.

clue.text: Lower taking last part of soup

parts.note: an ox lows, so it is a 'lower', one that moos
the tail is the end or rear part of something

explanation.surface: Something being lowered absorbs the final portion of a broth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like 'reduce' but is read as low-er, an animal that moos.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick soup made from the tail of cattle.

clue.text: Reluctant to produce a few lines

parts.note: a verse is a short group of lines in a poem

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to write a short poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to produce' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or unwilling, having a strong dislike for something.

clue.text: Cheerfully lively forecast?

definitions.meaning: describes a person's sunny, breezy manner
read literally as weather to come: sunny with a fresh wind

explanation.surface: A description of an upbeat person who sounds like the weather report.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal weather reading of a phrase normally used for personality.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an animated, cheery manner, and literally sunny weather with a stiff wind.

clue.text: Private papers mixed up

indicators.note: the letters of the word are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Confidential documents have been put in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' reads as 'confidential' but is the military rank; a sapper is a private soldier in the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is the lowest rank in the Royal Engineers, equivalent to a private soldier.

clue.text: Nora we mistook for another lady

indicators.note: the letters are got wrong, i.e. rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: We confused Nora with a different woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistook' rearranges NORAWE. Rowena is a woman's name, famous from Scott's novel Ivanhoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is a female first name, as borne by the Saxon heroine of Ivanhoe.

clue.text: Exactly like Kipling's stories

definitions.meaning: precisely, in just the right way
Rudyard Kipling's children's collection explaining how animals got their features

explanation.surface: A remark that something is precisely in the manner of a famous author's tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 1902 children's book of fanciful animal origin tales carries this phrase in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely or neatly arranged, and names Kipling's 1902 children's tales.

clue.text: Enlist Joanna with picture, not leading portrait

parts.note: Jo is a short form of the name Joanna

indicators.note: says the following letter is to be taken away from the word for picture

parts.note: a pin-up is a picture pinned to a wall

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is the one meant

explanation.surface: Joanna is told to sign up, with a photo but without the main portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' and 'portrait' look like a pair of synonyms, but 'leading portrait' is just its first letter, which 'not' removes from the pin-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up is to sign on with the armed forces, a common way of enlisting.

clue.text: Come into contact with leg and mention in passing

parts.note: to touch something is to be in contact with it
on is the leg side in cricket, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: A physio presses on a leg while chatting about it briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and leg side are the same half of the field, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch on a subject is to refer to it briefly without going into detail.

clue.text: Black in Kentucky

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky

explanation.surface: A dark colour found in a southern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black in Kentucky' looks like a statement about the state; it is IN plus KY.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means dark as ink, so jet-black in colour.

clue.text: Pronounced defect

parts.note: 'pronounced' looks like 'marked' but means spoken, so this is a fault in speech

explanation.surface: A strikingly obvious flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' usually means 'very noticeable'; here it is a defect in how sounds are pronounced, sibilants in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment where s and z are sounded like th is a fault in articulation.

clue.text: Seaweed covering two thirds of the fungus

indicators.note: only the front two thirds of the word for the fungus are taken, so its last third is dropped

parts.note: an agaric is a gill fungus such as the field mushroom

explanation.surface: Marine algae growing over most of a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: AGARIC has six letters; its first two thirds, four letters, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly extracted from red seaweed, and the name extends to the algae themselves.

clue.text: Determining the order of most of the dancing in middle of night

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the dance word is used

parts.note: sequence dancing is a British ballroom style where couples perform set steps in unison

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word is taken

explanation.surface: Working out the running order for a late-night dance session.
explanation.walkthrough: Sequence dancing is a British ballroom style; SEQUENC plus IN plus G (the centre of 'night') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequencing is arranging items in a particular order, as in reading genetic code base by base.

clue.text: Average man

definitions.meaning: A man's name, short for Norman

explanation.surface: A description of an ordinary chap.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the usual standard, the other a male first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a typical standard or average, and Norm is a male first name.

clue.text: Basket's contents not wanted

parts.note: describes the discarded sheets that fill an office bin for unwanted documents

explanation.surface: A note that the things in a basket are unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket' suggests a shopping basket; it is the office bin for discarded documents.
explanation.definitionFit: This is discarded sheets and documents, as thrown into an office bin.
